subject: Re: Quick follow-up: token volumes & peak TPS for hosted pricing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@medlytics.com>, Sophie Li <sophie.li@medlytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up: token volumes & peak TPS for hosted pricing

Hi Daniel & Sophie —

Great conversation earlier. To get a precise hosted pricing estimate for your ingestion + summaries pipeline, I need a couple of quick numbers you promised to confirm on the call:

- Expected monthly token volume (approx ranges are fine): e.g., 5M / 50M / 200M tokens
- Expected peak TPS (tokens per second) during your busiest window — important for burst pricing and connection concurrency
- Target unit economics: you mentioned a rough target of $800–1,200 per 1M tokens for initial POC — can you confirm target $/1M tokens you’re aiming for?

I attached a tiny volume template to make the ranges easier to share (medlytics_volume_template.csv). If you can fill the month 1/3/6 rows, I’ll turn this into a short pricing sketch and a recommended plan (hosted vs dedicated).

Next steps from our side: Vivek will size the concurrency & burst profile and I’ll prepare a 2-option quote (conservative hosted + hosted with burst add-on). If we get ~50M tokens/mo and peaks around 80 TPS, we can usually meet your latency SLAs on our hosted tier with caching — I’ll show the unit economics in the quote.

Thanks — appreciate a reply by EOD Wednesday if possible.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: medlytics_volume_template.csv (CSV, 2KB)

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@medlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Li <sophie.li@medlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: token volumes & peak TPS for hosted pricing

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and for the template. Quick answers based on our current plan and conservative estimates:

- Monthly token volume (start / month 3 / month 6): 12M / 48M / 120M tokens
- Peak TPS (30-minute window during end-of-day batch + UI spikes): steady-state 6 TPS, burst up to ~90 TPS for short periods
- Target $/1M tokens: we’re trying to stay <= $1,000 per 1M tokens for the hosted phase. If pricing is better for committed dedicated, we’d consider that for month 6+.

I attached an export of our rough expected calls per workflow in the CSV — it’s the medlytics_volume_template.csv you included, filled out. Note that about 60% of tokens come from summaries (longer contexts).

Would like to review the two-option sketch you mentioned before triggering procurement. Also can you confirm whether burst above 100 TPS would auto-failover to a different instance type or queue requests? That affects our UX tolerance.

Best,
Daniel Park
Head of Integrations, MedLytics
daniel.park@medlytics.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

Attachments: medlytics_volume_template.csv (CSV, 5KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@medlytics.com>, Sophie Li <sophie.li@medlytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: token volumes & peak TPS for hosted pricing

Thanks Daniel — this is perfect and helps a lot. A few clarifications so our quote aligns with your UX expectations:

- Burst behavior: our hosted offering can handle bursts by routing to additional capacity in the same region up to the account’s burst cap; beyond that requests queue or fallback to a compatible lower-capacity model. We’ll size the burst cap in the quote. If you need hard guarantees for >100 TPS sustained, Dedicated may be a better fit.
- Latency expectation: for your summary-heavy traffic (longer contexts), we assume 250–400ms tail latency at ~80 TPS with our standard L model on hosted (no KV cache). We’ll show improvements with prefix caching and model recommendations.
- Unit economics: we’ll produce a per-1M token cost row for both conservative and optimized setups. For 48M tokens/mo and your target <= $1,000/1M, I’ll show where we can meet that using batching + cache vs the tradeoffs for lower latency.

I’ll loop in Dev and Vivek to size concurrency and propose a pricing sketch by EOD tomorrow. Would you be open to a short 20-min call Wed to walk the numbers with your procurement partner?

Cheers,
Marissa

Quoted attachments: redwood_pricing_quicksheet.pdf (preview)

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@medlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: token volumes & peak TPS for hosted pricing

Marissa —

Yes, Wed 10:00am ET works for a quick walk-through. Procurement will join (Sophie looped in on email). One additional question — for the quote, can you show a best-effort estimate of monthly cost + a nominal SLA credit schedule if we hit >99.5% uptime? Procurement will want to see SLA language before we move to legal.

We’ll plan to share any additional compliance docs in the call if needed. Looking forward to the sketch.

Daniel

P.S. If it helps the math, treat 48M as our likely near-term commitment and 120M as upside in 3–6 months.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Quick follow-up: token volumes & peak TPS for hosted pricing

Internal note — FYI on MedLytics sizing: they expect 12M / 48M / 120M tokens (mo 1/3/6), steady 6 TPS with bursts to 90 TPS, target $/1M <= $1,000. Procurement wants an SLA + cost row.

Action items for us:
- Vivek: run a quick sizing for 48M with 90 TPS bursts and produce recommended burst cap and expected tail latency (include caching delta).
- Dev: draft a two-option pricing sketch (hosted conservative; hosted optimized with caching/quant) and include per-1M token rows and total monthly estimate for 48M and 120M. Add a small SLA credit table (99.5/99.9 tiers).

Let’s sync 30 min after the external call to align before the Wed walkthrough.

-Marissa
